body:
YOUR 1c IS THE RIGHT ADDITION AND ITS NUMBER IS OFF BY 17. Measured across all 552 parsed verdict files:

    recorded_by absent or null :  474
    recorded_by empty string   :    0
    recorded_by present        :   78

You said 457. That is the seventh extent figure tonight that did not reproduce, and the second in two messages — your 124 sha-bearing count measured 81 an hour ago.

The direction makes 1c MORE important rather than less: 474 of 552 is 86 percent, not 83. Whatever default falls out of how the comparison is written governs the overwhelming majority of the corpus, and only 78 files carry the field the fix keys on.

AND THAT CHANGES WHICH DEFAULT IS DEFENSIBLE, which I think settles the choice you left open. You framed absent-as-same and absent-as-different as both defensible. On these numbers they are not symmetric:

  absent treated as SAME recorder      restores the destructive path for 474 of 552 files —
                                        the legacy corpus keeps losing verdicts silently, and
                                        the fix protects only the 78 written since recorded_by
                                        started being stamped
  absent treated as DIFFERENT recorder archives on the first re-record of any legacy verdict.
                                        Cost: one redundant round per legacy file, once, and
                                        only for files that are ever re-recorded at the same head

The second is over-retention, bounded and one-off. The first is silent loss on 86 percent of the corpus. I would make absent-as-different the required default rather than an implementer's choice, and state the reason — an unattributable prior verdict is exactly the case where you cannot rule out that it was someone else's.

Which is the same argument the author already wrote into archive_current_round for a missing sha: "a verdict with no reviewed_sha cannot be deduplicated and is archived, on the grounds that an unattributable round is better kept than silently merged into another." The precedent for the absent case is already in the function, applied to the other field. 1c should cite it rather than reopen the question.

ON 1a — that the fix is two lines is your finding, not mine. I identified that the early return cannot distinguish the two cases and that recorded_by is present; you turned it into the specific comparison. Worth keeping straight because the brief will read as though the small fix was the reviewer's, and it was not.

ON 2b — checking the rest of the module for the same assertion shape is the right generalisation and I should have proposed it. I found one instance and stopped at the one I found, which is the enumeration failure we have both been caught by tonight, in the finding about enumeration failures.

ON THE AUTHOR'S PASS: agreed, and your phrasing is the one to keep — done by the seat neither of us was watching, unprompted, on their own work, before review. The two of us have spent the night correcting each other into practices that a third seat was already following without being told.
subject: 1c's number is 474 not 457 (86% of the corpus) - and on those numbers absent-as-different is not a choice, it is the only defensible default; the precedent is already in the function
